reporting-org.narrative: Siasa Place (SP) is a civic-tech youth-led non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 2015 that specializes in working with grassroots youth, in building institutional structures to support youth participation in politics and good governance. SP targets youth (men and women aged 18 to 35 years) and develops their skills in policy review, supporting the creation of youth-friendly platforms for public participation in decision-making processes, including the budget process and social accountability. SP works in 12 counties including Uasin Gishu, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori, Kericho, Nakuru, Nairobi, Kitui, Lamu, and Mombasa.

title.narrative: Strengthening the Power of Youth Voices quarterly report Jan 2023 - March 2023

description.narrative: During this reporting period, the project facilitated nine online and offline forums that reached over 32,000 individuals—31,840 through social media and 837 through physical engagements. These interactions allowed youth to articulate civic and governance issues specific to their counties. As a result, the project witnessed growing youth participation in local governance. Trained youth leaders initiated and submitted three petitions, ran two impactful online campaigns addressing access to education and the cost of living, and achieved tangible outcomes such as the construction of public toilets in response to their advocacy. A notable milestone was the establishment of “Offices of the Citizen” in Homa Bay, Busia, and Kericho. In Homa Bay, a local youth organization, County Voice and Rights, donated space for this office, which now receives complaints and facilitates advocacy. Three petitions have been formally presented through this office. Busia and Kericho county governments have also offered office space to support the initiative. These offices serve as institutionalized spaces for sustained youth-government dialogue and accountability efforts. The program’s impact was further demonstrated through increased youth initiative and leadership. In Homa Bay, youth submitted petitions addressing waste management and livestock control. Kericho youth filed a legal petition on public participation, while Busia youth played an active role in shaping the County Integrated Development Plan (CIDP). Youth across the counties also led social media campaigns on pressing issues and are preparing new initiatives, such as advocating for improved healthcare services. To ensure sustainability, the project was implemented through strong partnerships with county-based youth organizations. These partnerships facilitated mentorship, local ownership, and ongoing oversight through a project steering committee. Monitoring and evaluation mechanisms guided responsive programming, ensuring that youth-led strategies remained relevant and effective. Overall, the quarter demonstrated meaningful progress in institutionalizing youth voices in governance, building capacity, and fostering inclusive civic engagement platforms
